action: Apply the Broadcom fix (VMSA-2026-0009; e.g. vCenter 8.0 U3m) now; Broadcom lists no workaround. Restrict inbound access and egress from vCenter, and hunt with the GTIG indicators.

attribution.claim: Suspected PRC-nexus espionage actor ARMORY CASTLE (formerly UNC5221)

exec: A suspected state-backed group used an unpatched vCenter flaw to control virtualisation hosts, which hold most servers in a company; the fix is available now.
plain: Google says a suspected China-linked spy group exploited a previously unknown flaw in VMware vCenter to take control of virtual server infrastructure. A patch is out.

key_findings: CVE-2026-123890 in vCenter Server is an unauthenticated SRP-6a session key disclosure over DCE/RPC leading to authentication bypass as administrator@vsphere.local; Broadcom patch page linked from the post.
The campaign used two zero-days in total; the other is the BeyondTrust Remote Support flaw CVE-2026-102764 from GTIG's 15 October post.
The actor moved from a BeyondTrust appliance to internal Linux appliances without EDR, then to vCenter and ESXi.
Five newly identified malware families and utilities are described, including the SLIMSAVAGE and CAGEMATCH webshells, the BEARBONES backdoor, BONESAW and SAWSNAKE; LAZYBONES was also deployed.
The post names no victim organisations or countries.
recommendations: Use the Mandiant VCSA Hardening and Logging Tool after testing and change control.
Hunt with the YARA rules and indicators in the GTI collection.

summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group says ARMORY CASTLE, a suspected PRC-nexus espionage actor it formerly tracked as UNC5221, exploited CVE-2026-123890, an unauthenticated authentication bypass in VMware vCenter Server disclosed on 19 November. Rapid7 reports a CVSS of 9.8, exploitation from as early as September, fixes in vCenter 8.0 U3m and other builds, and no workaround. No victims are named.
title: Google: ARMORY CASTLE exploits vCenter zero-day CVE-2026-123890 in espionage campaign
